column1: # HeartBreaker: what Objective-See says it does. Only what the article states; written before the capture was read.
# Source: https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x8A.html ("Heartbreaker: Metamorphic ransomware comes for macOS", Patrick Wardle, 2026-10-18).
# The lab sample (objective-see/malware HeartBreaker.zip, file HeartBreaker/heartbreaker, ad-hoc signed arm64 Mach-O, codesign
# identifier heartbreaker-e2c97a640967e3f6, sha256 6bdf42a575d2daee3de2530161cb5b1fef6ca78b4abfa74f329d6b6c72890d18) is the article's
# own sample: the sha256 is the VirusTotal ID the article links. The article states no MITRE ATT&CK IDs, so the mitre column says
# "not stated". It states no network activity, so none is expected. The persistence row names persistence-item (a launch item
# registered with the background task manager); persistence-plist is the rule for a plist written with no registration event.
# The encryption row first had `-` (no rule): the run showed that gap, and mass-rename was written for it. The rule is now named here.
Writes a LaunchAgent plist (~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.network.startup.plist, RunAtLoad) that runs its own binary at login
Encrypts every file under ~/Downloads with AES-256-GCM (truncates the original, writes nonce, ciphertext and tag) and renames it to add .heartbreaker
Writes a ransom note named README.txt on the Desktop
Installs Rust (cargo) when it is missing; the article does not say how
Builds a modified copy of itself with cargo build --release in a temporary project, then renames its running executable and copies the new build into place (metamorphism)
